correctness.rationale: The overlap graph has distinct triples of degree two and triples aba of degree d=q−2, with equal indegree and outdegree. Rotation and the route abc→bcb→cba generate all permutations of a support; the same route can replace a with any letter outside {b,c}, giving strong connectivity for all q≥3. With row adjacency, the three transfer actions are SQ=X, SRQ=Y, SR²Q=dJ. Each triple rotation orbit has size three, so the Schur complement has the stated power of A³−1, which is nonzero at z=0. The pair residual after constants and row/column letter functions has both row and column sums zero. Its symmetric and skew dimensions follow from unsigned complete-graph incidence of rank q (an odd triangle forces any left-kernel vector to vanish) and oriented incidence of rank q−1 (the left kernel is constant). On those spaces X=Y=−I, and J=±I. On the 2×2 letter block the determinant at zero is (3d+2)(5d+4)−(4−d)(2−d)=14dq, repeated q−1 times. The constant factor is z(z+d+1)(A²+A+1), so it contributes derivative 7(q−1); the symmetric and skew factors at zero are 6(q−1) and 2(4q−5). Divide the derivative of the full determinant by q(q−1)², since the balanced strongly connected graph has equal in-arborescence cofactors. BEST with a specified first edge multiplies this cofactor by ((q−3)!)^{q(q−1)}. Every cycle has exactly one rotation with that edge first; neither reversal nor relabeling was divided out. At q=3 the symmetric summand is zero-dimensional, the derivative is 144, and the cofactor and the cycle count are both 12.
